solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Craze coming over to British part of Canada

indicators.note: the craze word is draped over the next pieces, so it wraps around them

parts.note: a craze or obsession is a mania
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fad crosses the Atlantic to the British-settled part of Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: This prairie province is one of the ten provinces making up the Canadian federation.

clue.text: Around the outskirts of Dundee, not all is quiet

indicators.note: the word for nearly everything goes around the edge letters of the Scottish city

parts.note: not all but nearly so is most

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of Dundee

explanation.surface: Around the edges of Dundee, things are mostly but not entirely peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quiet' looks like part of the picture of Dundee, but it is the definition, in its sense of unassuming.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiet in the sense of unassuming or retiring is a synonym for this adjective.

clue.text: Ultimate in madmen, say?

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so take the last letter of madmen

parts.note: to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: Someone is held up as the extreme example of a lunatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimate in' takes N, the final letter of madmen; the whole clue then doubles as a jokey description of the answer, the ultimate madman.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for a crazy person, the most extreme of madmen.

clue.text: Error clear after a turnaround in sport

indicators.note: a turnaround turns things the other way, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing or error
to clear a sum as profit is to net it

explanation.surface: A mistake is cleared up after a game changes course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a turnaround' reverses SINNET into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This racket game played over a net is a well-known sport.

clue.text: Wife — one taking a chance on small beer

parts.note: someone who gambles or takes a chance is a better
a half is a half-pint, the small measure of beer in a British pub

explanation.surface: A wife is described as a gambler who drinks modest beers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs a 'half' is a half-pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous idiom for one's spouse, especially a wife, is 'my better half'.

clue.text: Interstellar measure in space worked out about right

indicators.note: the reworked letters go about, that is around, the abbreviation for right
worked out means rearranged or solved, so the letters of space are shuffled

explanation.surface: A unit of interstellar distance is calculated out in space, roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges SPACE into PASEC; 'about' puts it around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of astronomical distance of about 3.26 light years, used between stars.

clue.text: Inspiring type partial to foxtrot — am I naturally uplifting?

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up means reading the letters bottom to top, backwards
partial means only part of, so a piece of these words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone inspiring asks whether a fondness for the foxtrot is naturally uplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial to' looks like 'fond of', but signals a hidden run, ROTAMINA, which 'uplifting' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who animates others brings them life and spirit, an inspiring sort of person.

clue.text: Wave as saline as a salt-water creature

indicators.note: to wave is to move back and forth, so the letters are stirred about

explanation.surface: An ocean wave is as salty as a sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' rearranges AS SALINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine gastropod mollusc living in salt water is a kind of creature of the sea.

clue.text: Go shortly into jail that's split down the middle

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, so the shortened word is placed inside the jail

parts.note: a cage is a prison or jail

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go to prison briefly, a cell divided in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts LEAVE to LEAV, which goes 'into' CAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleavage is a division or split, such as the hollow between breasts or a rock's split.

clue.text: Give hosts extra time to set off

indicators.note: to host is to have inside, so the donating word contains the abbreviation

parts.note: to give money is to donate
ET is the football abbreviation for extra time

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to grant hosts more time to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give hosts' reads as giving to hosts, but 'hosts' is the container signal. In football, extra time is the added period after a drawn match.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb or charge is to make it explode.

clue.text: Fight to mask droop in face

indicators.note: a mask covers something, so the fight word goes around the droop word

parts.note: to vie is to contend or fight
to sag is to droop

explanation.surface: A struggle hides a sagging face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mask' tempts as a link to 'face', but here it means cover, so one piece wraps the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A visage is a literary synonym for one's countenance.

clue.text: A thousand breaking pieces shattering, then an indefinite number, for example

indicators.note: the thousand breaks into the rearranged letters, sitting inside them
shattering smashes things up, so the letters of pieces are scrambled

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
in maths n stands for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A thousand smashed bits, then countless more, are given as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattering' rearranges PIECES to SPECIE, and 'breaking' places M inside it before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a sample or instance, a single example of its kind.

clue.text: Travel guide not entirely relevant, a sucker being sent the wrong way

indicators.note: sent the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
only part of the words is used, so a run of letters is taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A navigation device is somewhat irrelevant, a mug getting misdirected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' takes VANTAS from 'relevant, a sucker'; 'being sent the wrong way' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite navigation device in a car guides travellers along their route.

clue.text: Old queen pens dirge composed on old instrument

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the queen's name holds the rearranged letters

parts.note: Dido was the legendary queen of ancient Carthage

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters of dirge are reordered

explanation.surface: An ancient queen writes a lament to be played on a primitive instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' gives DGERI, which 'pens' encloses; 'on' adds the final O.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aboriginal Australian wind instrument, a long wooden drone pipe.

clue.text: Team entering biathlon, fifty missing out on good sport

indicators.note: the team goes into the shortened winter-sport word
out means not in order, so the combined letters are rearranged
missing means lacking, so the letter for fifty is taken away

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a football or cricket side

explanation.surface: A squad enters a biathlon minus some competitors, missing out on a fine contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' leaves BIATHON; 'out' rearranges it with the team into THAIBOXIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Muay Thai, the kickboxing martial art of Thailand, is a combat sport.

clue.text: Student's first securing work on the web

indicators.note: the first letter of the student word is taken

parts.note: securing something with pins is pinning it

explanation.surface: A student's first job is fastening things down on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work on the web' suggests the internet, but a spider spins its web.
explanation.definitionFit: Making thread for a web is what a spider does, a punning sense of web-work.

clue.text: Crazy jokes in these

definitions.meaning: informal British word for mad or insane
British Christmas party favours, pulled with a bang, hold paper hats and corny jokes

explanation.surface: Mad jokes are found inside these.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: slang for mad, and the festive tubes that contain jokes.

clue.text: I live beneath female domestic

indicators.note: in a down clue beneath means placed below, so the female letter comes first

parts.note: to live somewhere is to reside there

explanation.surface: Someone lives below a woman, in a household setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside stands for home life, so it serves as an adjective meaning homely or domestic.

clue.text: Frivolous talk from servant carrying rifles around

indicators.note: the servant carries, that is contains, the rearranged letters

parts.note: a page is a boy servant or attendant

indicators.note: around means all over the place, so the letters of rifles are mixed up

explanation.surface: Light banter comes from a servant lugging guns around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' gives ERSIFL, which the servant is 'carrying'.
explanation.definitionFit: Persiflage is light, mocking banter, a flippant style of conversation.

clue.text: Develop program with attention

parts.note: an app is a computer program
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Someone builds software that commands notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop in the sense of emerging or coming into view is to show up.

clue.text: Rookie unable to get a grip?

definitions.meaning: a rookie is a beginner or learner
having ..., the gripping tool on a workbench, so read as two words

explanation.surface: A newcomer cannot yet get to grips with things.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: split as NO VICE, someone lacks a vice to grip with.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a beginner, a newcomer to some activity.

clue.text: As medicine taken, zero needing to get better

parts.note: O looks like zero
to rally is to recover or improve

explanation.surface: A patient on nothing needs to recover, with medicine to be swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicine taken by mouth is administered this way, in contrast to injection.

clue.text: Thief in pound

definitions.meaning: one who nicks, that is steals, things
British slang for one pound sterling

explanation.surface: A robber is inside the police pound.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for someone who steals, and British slang for a pound coin or note.

clue.text: Hole in floor, reverse cross-section

indicators.note: reverse means turn round, so the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix or cross, as on a church rood screen
a part is a section

explanation.surface: A hole in the floor shows a cutaway view in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross-section' looks like one term but splits into two pieces; 'reverse' turns ROODPART round.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged flap covering an opening in a floor or ceiling is this kind of door.

clue.text: Two nations — or one without leader?

indicators.note: without the leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: one refers to a single nation, the West African country Liberia

explanation.surface: A riddle asks whether this is two countries or one lacking a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' means one nation, LIBERIA, and 'without leader' drops its L.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula of southwest Europe holds Spain and Portugal, two countries.

clue.text: Slowly advance with an inclination for battle

parts.note: to edge forward is to move slowly
a hill is a slope or incline

explanation.surface: Creeping forward with a taste for combat.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgehill (1642) was the first major battle of the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: This English Civil War engagement in Warwickshire is a famous battle.

clue.text: Initially, girl guide is well

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of girl

parts.note: an usher guides people to their seats

explanation.surface: At first a girl guide is in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl guide' reads as a Guide (Girl Scout), but it splits: G from girl, then USHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusher is an oil well that spouts freely, so a noun sense of well.

clue.text: Thus French produce case of therapy in moderation

parts.note: thus means so
Brie is a soft cheese made in France

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: French goods are offered as therapy, taken in moderation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes TY, the outside letters of therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobriety is temperance or restraint, especially in drinking.
